Biomedical and Environmental Health Sciences (PhD)
Admission to the Program
In addition to meeting the minimum university requirements for graduate study, applicants must submit a completed graduate application form, three letters of recommendation, and copies of all college transcripts.
Degree Requirements
41 credit hours of approved graduate work, exclusive of BEHS-898 Doctoral Continuing Enrollment (1-9) /BEHS-899 Doctoral Dissertation (9)
Comprehensive Exam: A student, with the help of his/her advisor, chooses a topic for specialization and forms a committee of at least four members (including the advisor), at least two of whom are full-time faculty at American University. The student is given a written or oral examination on this topic prepared and scored by the committee members. A student who fails the comprehensive examination may apply to the program director for one additional attempt
Research Assurances and Research Ethics Training: Appropriate protocol review and oversight of faculty and student research is an essential component of Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training on campus. All graduate students who are conducting research in partial fulfillment of a doctoral dissertation are required to participate in RCR training. Application forms and guidelines are available on AU's Research website. Copies of research assurances must be presented to the BEHS Director with the completed dissertation proposal
Advancement to Candidacy: Students are considered "advanced to candidacy" (or "all-but-dissertation") when they have completed all required course credits, have passed their comprehensive exam, and have an approved dissertation proposal
Dissertation:
​Committee Approval: Subject to applicable university academic regulations, students must obtain approval for the composition of the committee, normally in the third year. Committees must also include members from at least two different disciplines (e.g., Environmental Science and Chemistry)
Proposal Defense: Students develop an original research idea and present a proposal, orally, before their research committee, normally at the end of the third year
​Oral Dissertation Defense: When the actual dissertation is nearly finished, an oral defense of the complete draft dissertation is held. The oral defense includes the dissertation committee as well as an outside member that meets the qualifications as stipulated in the applicable university academic regulations. Final approval of the dissertation depends on satisfactory completion of any changes required by the committee members following the oral defense. Dissertations are subject to all applicable university regulations

BEHS-701 Molecules to Organisms (3)
BEHS-702 Organisms to Ecosystems (3)

BIO-697 Research Methodology in Biology (3)
CHEM-602 Research Method Design (3)
ENSC-682 Research Methods in Environmental Science (3)
Statistical Analysis and Computation (3 credit hours)

DATA-612 Statistical Programming in R (3)
STAT-614 Statistical Methods (3)
STAT-615 Regression (3)
STAT-616 Generalized Linear Models (3)
STAT-622 Advanced Biostatistics (3)
Electives (9 credit hours)
Biomedical

BEHS-710 Sustainable Systems of Drug Development: One Health Initiative (3)
BIO-655 Endocrinology (3)
BIO-685 Bioinformatics (3)
BIO-687 Principles of Genomics (3)
BIO-688 Virology (3)
BIO-689 Biotechnology (3)
CHEM-624 Application of Spectroscopy in Medicinal Chemistry (3)
CHEM-633 Protein Chemistry (3)
CHEM-636 Clinical Laboratory: Analysis, Quality Assurance and Control (3)
CHEM-642 Chemical and Enzyme Kinetics (3)
CHEM-650 Bioinorganic Chemistry (3)
Environmental and Health Science

BIO-626 Molecular Epidemiology (3)
CHEM-605 Separation Science (3)
CHEM-606 Trace Analysis (3)
CHEM-662 Topics in Environmental Chemistry (3)
ENSC-500 Ecohydrology (3)
ENSC-505 Energy (3)
ENSC-624 Environmental Health (3)
/ HLTH-624 Environmental Health (3)
ENSC-630 Environmental Modeling (3)

ENSC-665 Environmental Risk Assessment and Global Green Transformation (3)
ENSC-670 Water Resources (3)

Arctic Climate Change
Urban Bird Conservation
ENSC-685 Remote Sensing: Environmental Measurement from Satellites and Drones (3)
ENSC-696 Selected Topics: Non-Recurring (1-6)
Policy and Regulatory
Complete 3 credit hours from the following:
CHEM-679 Countering Chemical Weapons (3)
ISCI-601 Communicating Science to the Public (3)
PUAD-603 Policy Process (3)
PUAD-606 Foundations of Policy Analysis (3)
PUAD-617 Project Management (3)
PUAD-685 Topics in Policy Analysis and Management (1-3) : Regulatory Policy and Management
SIS-660 Environment and Politics (3)

Activism, Engagement, and Social Movements
Climate Change Policy
Environmental Justice
Political Ecology of Food and Agriculture
Water Governance
SIS-635 Advanced Topics in Development Management (3) : Program Planning in Global Health
Lab Rotation (3 credit hours)
BEHS-720 Lab Rotation (3)
Directed Research (12 credit hours)
Complete 12 credit hours from the following:
BEHS-698 Directed Research (1-9)
Research Seminar (5 credit hours)
BEHS-680 Proseminar on the Integration of Science and Policy (3)
BEHS-681 Seminar in Biomedical and Environmental Health Sciences (1) (2 credit hours required)
Dissertation
